description: Figure 7 (bottom plot) illustrates accuracy as a function of subject popularity, showing two accuracy curves across binned values of \(s\_pop\). The x-axis is labeled “s_pop frequency (x10^4)” on a linear scale, with tick labels at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, and 19 (range 1–19). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” on a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0, with regularly spaced ticks at 0.2 intervals. Two lines are plotted: a green solid line with square markers labeled “Initial Accuracy,” which starts near 0.35 at \(s\_pop=1\), rises to around 0.6 by \(s\_pop\approx 5\), fluctuates around roughly 0.5–0.65 through \(s\_pop\approx 15\), and ends at approximately 1.0 at \(s\_pop=19\); and a blue dashed line with circular markers labeled “Final Accuracy,” which begins around 0.85 at \(s\_pop=1\), stays close to 0.9–1.0 across most x-values with a small dip around \(s\_pop\approx 15\), and finishes near 1.0 at \(s\_pop=19\). Vertical error bars are shown on the green series at each x-position, with visibly larger bars at several mid-range points (e.g., around \(s\_pop\approx 9\) and \(s\_pop\approx 13\)).
